text:
The failing fc is the main clue. The filter is a unity-gain Sallen-Key lowpass, and the simulated -3 dB point (63 MHz) matches the dominant pole of the actual network, about 1/[C2·(R1+R2)]. The sensitivities confirm this: C2 and R2 each give about -16% for +20%, while R1, C1, and Rz barely move fc. The target of 152 to 228 MHz needs roughly a 3x increase in fc, which points to an oversized C2 or R2.

Between the two, C2 is the more likely corrupted element. Its value (1.92e-13 F) is out of line with the other network values. R2 is a close second. The peaking failure comes from the amplifier (M4, Cc, M3, M8), not the passive network, so it is probably a separate issue. M5 being in triode is real but is unlikely to cause a 3x fc shortfall, since the tail current is consistent with the rest of the bias.

{"ranking": ["C2", "R2", "Cc"], "fault": "C2 is oversized (1.923e-13 F, roughly 3x the value needed). In this low-Q unity-gain Sallen-Key network fc is set by 1/(C2*(R1+R2)), so the -3 dB point drops to about 63 MHz instead of about 190 MHz. Reducing C2 to about 6e-14 F, or equivalently R2 by about 3x, would restore fc. The 2.96 dB peaking is a separate amplifier-compensation issue (Cc too small, M4 too large) and is not explained by this fault alone."}
